column7: the STRUCTURAL-ALLOCATION class (e13-b audit fix round R2, 2026-09-05, disposition (b); re-audit fix round R2'-1/R1'-3): a composite-literal / slice-literal allocation, an interface method value, or an ALLOCATING CONVERSION (`[]byte(s[i:j])` — its operand is the payload) whose payload can panic (`(&T{x: s[i]}).x + wit(5)`), followed by an ordered call/receive in the same statement. The allocation hoists to its lexical position and evaluates its payload THERE, ahead of the later event; gc evaluates the payload in the residual, after the call (it prints `wit 5` then panics; measured for the receive too: `[]int{s[i]}[0] + <-ch` receives first) — neither order is spec-forced (a literal is not a call) and the machine realizes only one, and no unseq-probe can reach gc's member (the allocation statement re-raises a deferred panic at the same early position). NOT refused: a MAP literal (gc's order.go OMAPLIT emits its dynamic entries as statements at the literal's position — the machine's member IS gc's: `map-lit-payload-vs-call` green), a literal inside the ARGUMENT subtree of an ordered call that precedes the next event (forced: `composite-ptr-in-arg-then-call` green), the no-event / event-inside-the-literal / variadic-pack shapes (`assert-composite-lit`, `index-composite-lit` green). Pre-existing on main (the hoist order was emission order there too), undisclosed under E13 until the audit; refused by name. Rows: `builtins/e13-sibling-panic-order/{composite-ptr-payload-vs-call,slice-lit-payload-vs-call,composite-ptr-payload-vs-call-printroot,slice-lit-payload-vs-call-sinkroot,slice-lit-payload-vs-recv,bytes-conv-payload-vs-call}` red by design (BUG-102's Cases line)
